description: Key terms and concepts used throughout the OpenTripMap API

terms.definition: Unique identifier of an object in OpenTripMap, typically prefixed with a source indicator (N for OpenStreetMap nodes, W for ways, R for relations).
Comma-separated list of hierarchical category tags classifying the type of point of interest. Over 150 categories are supported.
Popularity/importance rating of a POI on a scale where higher values indicate more notable places. Values: 1 (low), 2, 3 (medium), 4, 5, 6, 7 (high, UNESCO/top attractions).
ISO 639-1 two-letter language code specifying the language for returned descriptions and names.
Bounding box defined by minimum and maximum longitude/latitude coordinates used to spatially filter POI results.
Search radius in meters from a given center point (lon/lat) used to filter nearby POIs.
Filter results by geometry source. Accepted values include 'osm' (OpenStreetMap), 'wikidata', and others.
Filter results by attribute source, specifying which data sources must provide attributes for the returned objects.
Response format selector. Use 'json' for a JSON array of SimpleFeature objects or 'geojson' for a GeoJSON FeatureCollection.
The canonical OpenTripMap URL for a place's detail page.
OpenStreetMap identifier for the object, linking to the corresponding OSM element.
Wikidata entity identifier (Q-number) linking the POI to structured data in Wikidata.
Geographic coordinates object with 'lon' (longitude) and 'lat' (latitude) fields representing the location of a POI.
Object containing a Wikipedia summary for the POI including plain text and HTML versions of the excerpt.
Object containing a thumbnail image URL with width and height for display in list views.
In autosuggest responses, the matched name with the search term highlighted using HTML bold tags.
Geographic location resolved from a place name, returning coordinates and country information useful as a search center point.
